advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Propagate `registry_drift` from `compute_validity` through `claim_gate_check` and into the `plan_review_status` result (and `review-plan --status` output) so the documented drift visibility is actually delivered.
evidence: attest_gate.py:151 (claim_gate_check valid path): `return {"ok": True, "reason": "certified plan-review attestation", "verdict": "certified"}` — no `registry_drift` copied from `validity`
attest_gate.py:180-186 (plan_review_status): builds `status = {"ok":..., "verdict":..., "reason":..., "verified_at_sha": None, "signed_at": None}` with no `registry_drift` key

docs/adr/0053-grandfather-criteria-registry-drift.md:58-61: '...that field rides along on every verdict the call returns, so `review-plan --status` and the gate UX can still tell an operator the plan was reviewed under an older criteria registry.'
docs/plan-review-gate.md:473-475: 'surfaced as a non-blocking `registry_drift` on the result ... rather than invalidating the attestation'
advisory.finding: The `registry_drift` field is never propagated to the operator-facing surfaces (`plan_review_status` / `review-plan --status` / `claim_gate_check`), so the 'detected and reported, not discarded' guarantee of ADR 0053 is not actually delivered where an operator would see it.
scenarios: An operator runs `rebar review-plan <id> --status` (or `-o json`) on a ticket whose attestation predates a criteria tightening — the output shows `certified` with no indication the plan was reviewed under an older registry, contradicting the documented mitigation (visibility) that makes the accepted-cost tolerable.
advisory.suggested_fix: In claim_gate_check's valid-return (attest_gate.py:151) copy `validity.get("registry_drift")` into the returned dict when present, and in plan_review_status carry `gate.get("registry_drift")` into the status dict; then have _llm_commands render it in the text branch.

evidence: tests/unit/test_compute_validity.py: `def test_regver_drift_does_not_mask_other_staleness` monkeypatches only head_sha to 'headB' and asserts `res["verdict"] == "stale-head"` — the unscoped branch

ABSENCE: no test asserts a scoped attestation with a drifted dep AND a rotated regver returns `stale-code` while carrying `registry_drift`
advisory.finding: The commit claims a test drifts a dependency on a regver-skewed attestation and asserts `stale-code`, but the new non-masking test (`test_regver_drift_does_not_mask_other_staleness`) exercises only the UNSCOPED whole-HEAD path (asserts `stale-head`), not the scoped dependency-drift path that returns `stale-code`. No test co-locates registry drift with a scoped dep-drift, leaving the DEFAULT-profile `stale-code` branch (attest.py:677) untested for co-occurring `registry_drift`.
scenarios: A regression that lets registry-drift handling short-circuit or mask the scoped dep-hash re-check would slip past the suite while the unscoped head test still passes
